title: Shallow TVD reversals still escape the N/A pay convention
cause: The allowed negative difference is proportional to absolute TVD and applied separately to every grid step. At TVD 10,000 ft the per-step allowance is about 0.01 ft; a cumulative 10-ft rise spread over 2,000 samples passes. A finite grid also is not a proof over survey stations.
repro: Run probes/numerical_reference.py: MD 10000-12000, TVD 10000-9990, all samples pay. Repeat using the audit-built compiled pay extension.
expected: Any genuinely upward/reversing TVD interval follows the stated convention: TVD gross/net/N:G/products N/A, MD interval separate. Conventional controls unchanged.
observed: Gross 0 ft, net 10 ft, PhiH 2 ft, empty warning; MD interval 2000 ft. Same result from compiled extension. A second physically identical 50-ft-upturn survey is correctly N/A with 100-ft sample spacing but wrongly numeric net50 with 0.25-ft spacing.
recommendation: Check actual MD-ordered survey segments and use an appropriate absolute tolerance against cumulative reversal, not an allowance multiplied by grid resolution. Preserve the agreed N/A convention.
regression_risks: Nearly horizontal wells, unit scaling, plateaus, sparse/irregular stations, and conventional-well results need independent reference tests; do not introduce MD substitution.
classification: Confirmed incomplete correction of earlier FA-002

title: A failed close-generation write silently leaves stale-copy protection ineffective
cause: Generation stamping is an extra close-time transaction. A SQLite write lock makes it fail; close catches/logs the error and closes normally with the previous generation and handoff still valid.
repro: Run probes/sync_edges.py: commit a well edit, hold BEGIN IMMEDIATE on another connection, shorten the probe busy timeout to 50ms, close the Workbench DB, release lock, then restore the earlier same-generation copy.
expected: A failed handoff-generation step is surfaced and cannot certify the changed/older copy as current. Previously committed edits remain durable.
observed: Close returns normally; the committed edit exists, but generation remains 1. Replacing it with the older generation-1 file produces no stale/handoff warning. No immediate SQLite loss is alleged.
recommendation: Treat generation/handoff failure as an explicit incomplete close/publication outcome. Ensure a changed project cannot retain a matching old verification record, and require retry or a clear unverified state.
regression_risks: Multi-module connections on one PC, busy timeout, WAL checkpoint failure, concurrent close and crash recovery; preserve committed data and explicit Open Anyway semantics.
classification: Confirmed incomplete correction of earlier PI-005

title: Post-commit Map refresh failure leaves a saved shape draft that duplicates on retry
cause: The feature commits, then refresh_layers runs before _into_shape_layer returns success and finish clears the draft. A refresh exception preserves the already-saved draft.
repro: Run probes/map_postcommit.py: draw into a real temporary polygon layer, inject an exception only in refresh_layers, then retry Finish after refresh recovers.
expected: Once committed, the draft is acknowledged exactly once; a display failure does not invite repeating the insert.
observed: One feature is stored after the exception; state remains draw with 3 vertices. Retry stores a second identical feature. Original database-write failure controls are corrected.
recommendation: Separate committed-save acknowledgement from optional UI refresh; end the saved draft before refreshing and offer redraw retry without reinsertion.
regression_risks: Keep drafts on genuine save failure/Cancel, and preserve undo/redo and active-shape-layer behavior.
classification: Confirmed remaining failure path related to earlier PI-006

title: Overwrite No does not protect an imported project-owned LIC
cause: Project LIC synchronization always runs for small successful imports before the optional original-LIC rewrite path. When the input is that same project LIC, it is rewritten directly regardless of overwrite_lic.
repro: Run probes/lic_edges.py: import a log, edit its generated project LIC calibration and add a harmless extra metadata line, reimport that file with overwrite_lic=False.
expected: The selected input LIC remains byte-for-byte unchanged when No is chosen, or an explicit conflict is disclosed before modifying it.
observed: Input changed; extra line lost; no backup; lic_rewritten=False; no warning note. Registration update itself succeeds.
recommendation: Detect input/output path identity and stage/skip project-LIC synchronization or require explicit consent/backup. Enforce input preservation across every writer, not only rewrite_lic_image.
regression_risks: Project LIC paths, same-file aliases, automatic synchronization, permission failures and imported calibration must retain existing behavior.

title: Generated LICs lose Petra GROUP identity and fail same-name section round trips
cause: lic_section stores GROUP identity, but sync_raster_lic omits the group argument when exporting. Both sections become GROUP 0; ambiguous name matching runs before the exact own-lic_path fallback.
repro: Run group_roundtrip in probes/lic_edges.py: same well/image/name GR, GROUP 1 and GROUP 2, export automatic project LICs and plan their reimport.
expected: Section identity survives save/export/reimport, and each own LIC resolves to its known registration.
observed: Stored sections 1|gr and 2|gr export as groups 0 and 0. Both own LICs fail with two registrations could be this control file.
recommendation: Preserve the stored GROUP metadata in project LIC output; ensure exact identity is not lost behind an ambiguous fallback.
regression_risks: Older registrations without lic_section, renamed logs, multiple sections with identical labels and moved images.

title: Geo Save As copies before pending form edits are saved
cause: The snapshot/copy is made from committed DB data first. load_project then asks to save the original dirty form, so the saved edit is missing from the copy already created.
repro: Run probes/save_as.py with the existing synthetic GeoPendingEdits fixture. Set well name Edited Draft, Save As, answer Yes to the save question.
expected: The saved-as project contains the edits the user agreed to save, or Save As clearly refuses until they are resolved.
observed: Original stores Edited Draft; the newly opened copy stores Tab Well. The original retains the edit; the new copy is stale.
recommendation: Resolve/save pending editors before taking the copy and honor failures/Cancel. Copy a coherent accepted application state, not a pre-prompt DB snapshot.
regression_risks: Do not create/open an unintended partial copy after cancellation or save failure; test header, tab and child-editor edits and original/copy identities.

title: Valid JSON with malformed generation fields escapes project-open error handling
cause: JSON syntax/type at the top level is checked, but generation_seq is converted with int without validating its value. The raw ValueError is outside the ProjectError handlers.
repro: Run malformed_handoff in probes/sync_edges.py with generation_seq set to corrupt-but-valid-json.
expected: Treat malformed metadata as an unverified copy with an actionable warning and safe explicit-open path.
observed: Raw ValueError escapes rather than returning an UnverifiedProjectCopy problem. Project data is not modified by this failure.
recommendation: Validate handoff/accepted-record field types and ranges; convert failures into the existing unverified-copy contract.
regression_risks: Corrupt valid JSON, missing/negative/oversized fields and old handoff formats; do not silently accept an invalid record.

title: Recovery Access labels its own current schema as a newer application version
cause: Recovery KNOWN_SCHEMA remains 29 while the application supports/writes schema 31.
repro: Create/open a current synthetic database using Recovery Access and read notes (probes/sync_edges.py).
expected: Current schema is recognized; genuine newer schemas retain the conservative warning.
observed: A current v0.9.72 schema-31 project is said to be from a newer version. Reading remains possible and forensic originals are unchanged.
recommendation: Share a dependency-light schema version constant or keep a guarded consistency check so recovery and database metadata cannot drift.
regression_risks: Maintain recovery independence from normal migrating/writing database import paths and older/newer schema safety.

title: LIC Cancel is checked only between 1,000-file write batches
cause: Cancellation is tested at batch entry, not inside its per-file loop, so Cancel cannot stop after the current file. A last-batch request may never be reflected in report.cancelled.
repro: Run probes/lic_cancel_batch.py with 2,327 synthetic LICs; request cancellation at begin(2001), with and without a concurrent SQLite writer.
expected: Finish/rollback the current file safely, stop before the next file and report unprocessed files accurately.
observed: Unlocked: all 2327 added, cancelled count 0. Locked with 10ms probe busy timeout: first 2000 stored, all remaining 327 attempted/failed over 4.33s, cancelled count 0.
recommendation: Check cancellation at each safe per-file boundary inside the batch; commit only completed items consistently and count remaining work. Distinguish database waits from parsing and UI refresh.
regression_risks: Do not abort an active file halfway, lose completed imports, rewrite LICs for rolled-back items, or misreport skipped versus cancelled records.
classification: Confirmed code defect; screenshot cause remains unverified

title: First-N-month production includes adjustments before first production
cause: The window predicate is m < n and lacks m >= 0, although offsets are relative to the first producing month. Negative-volume adjustments before that month are included in first-N totals.
repro: Run probes/production_edges.py: Dec2019 -100 bbl, Jan2020 200, Feb100, Mar100, same source.
expected: First production Jan2020; first 3 months Jan-Mar total 400. Overall cumulative may correctly include all history and equal 300.
observed: first_month is Jan2020 but first3_oil is 300, including the preceding December correction.
recommendation: Constrain the first-N window to 0 <= month_offset < N while leaving actual cumulative history unchanged.
regression_risks: Reported zeros, pre-production adjustments, gaps, source priority and incomplete histories; do not discard legitimate corrections globally.

title: Production import accepts non-finite volumes as successful numeric data
cause: float conversions accept infinity/overflow and no finite-value validation or problem is recorded before storage.
repro: Run nonfinite_import in probes/production_edges.py with oil=1e999.
expected: Reject/report invalid non-finite volumes without treating them as a measured monthly quantity.
observed: One row added, no problems, stored oil Infinity and cumulative oil Infinity.
recommendation: Validate finite numeric inputs and conversion results and report the offending row/column; keep missing data distinct from invalid values.
regression_risks: Existing null markers, legitimate negative adjustments, large finite volumes and update/replace transaction semantics.

title: Cross Section retains IDs of completed scheduled callbacks until close
cause: later adds every after/idle ID to _jobs but successful callbacks never remove their completed IDs. Destruction eventually clears the history.
repro: Run probes/section_jobs.py: schedule/drain 1000 no-op callbacks in one real synthetic Cross Section window.
expected: The active-job collection tracks pending jobs rather than growing with historical completed work.
observed: All 1000 callbacks complete, _jobs grows from 5 to1005 while only one Tcl callback remains pending. This retains strings, not the callback function graphs.
recommendation: Remove each completed job ID in an owner-safe wrapper/finally, preserving cancellation and disposal checks.
regression_risks: Cancelled, failed and nested callbacks and close ordering; no evidence ties this bookkeeping issue to SIGSEGV.

title: Petro successful-save reporting hides stale published zone results
cause: Zone publication failure rolls back its savepoint but is logged and swallowed; the accepted Petro state commits and save_project reports True with no partial-save warning.
repro: Run probes/petro_partial_publish.py: save a 60ft zone, extend base to5520 for80ft, inject an OperationalError only in publish_zone_values, save.
expected: Surface the partial publication failure and prevent old map/Geo zone values from appearing current for the newly accepted state.
observed: Stored zone base5520; published gross remains60 rather than80; save returnsTrue; no error/warning dialog; last_zone_refusals empty. Raw state survives.
recommendation: Propagate/record partial-publication status, retain a reliable retry and show stale/uncertain published results explicitly. Preserve accepted curve data while making the inconsistency visible.
regression_risks: Do not discard accepted raw curves, overwrite another producer, or turn a recoverable publication failure into silent data loss.

title: Current crash report incorrectly says Cross Section code is unchanged since v0.9.61
cause: The report extends a no-change assertion to Cross Section code, although commits in v0.9.62, v0.9.65 and v0.9.71 changed the window.
repro: Compare git log/diff for xsection/window.py; commit4a92878 changes persistence/close paths.
expected: Version-change statements distinguish unchanged tests from product paths actually changed.
observed: The current report says tests and Cross Section code unchanged since61. The v0.9.71 product delta disproves the latter; no causal crash regression is inferred.
recommendation: Correct the evidence statement and retain an exact changed-file/commit ledger.
regression_risks: Keep original crash evidence and clearly label historical versus current test/code revisions.

title: LIC progress claims success for a whole batch that rolled back
cause: Per-file success counters are incremented before the batch commits and are not reconciled after a commit failure. The detailed Report correctly marks errors, but the visible tally remains successful.
repro: Run probes/lic_commit_progress.py with two files, a real ProgressWindow and a failing commit wrapper.
expected: Final success/failure tallies and heading reflect committed outcomes consistently with the detailed report.
observed: Zero database rows; Report has0 added/2 errors, but the visible tally says Succeeded2 Failed0 and heading Completed. The detailed summary does disclose the two errors.
recommendation: Reconcile progress counters after batch commit/rollback and label completion with errors accurately; distinguish provisional processed work from durable additions.
regression_risks: Keep per-file savepoints, summary details and partial-batch cancellation accounting consistent.
introduced: Introduced by v0.9.72 write-batch progress flow

title: Intermittent Tk SIGSEGV remains an open release-stability gate
function: Tk update during Cross Section reopen
cause: The supplied current release report records an exit139 fault in Tk8.6 during the settings reopen test. No native root cause has been established. A passing later run does not close the fault.
repro: Use the original full order/runtime and a native debugger. This audit independently runs the complete available source suite once under gdb; see final Audit_Evidence for its actual outcome.
expected: Long GUI sessions complete without native fault; closure rests on a captured/understood reproducer, not selected green reruns.
observed: Supplied v0.9.72 evidence: Tk8.6 run1 crashed, then Tk9 and Tk8.6 passed. Those are author-supplied results, separate from this audit run. The original cause remains unresolved.
evidence: full-serial/pytest-native.log; docs/v0.9.72/LIC_Import_Test_Results.md; prior focused Tk audit
recommendation: Capture the native fault and correct the demonstrated owner/thread lifecycle path. Preserve traces and test order. Do not label the issue fixed merely because this audit run or a targeted run passes.
regression_risks: Windows impact and frozen executable behavior are unverified; do not presume a Linux Tcl panic is the same SIGSEGV.
confidence: High for supplied open crash; Low for exact root cause
classification: Supplied native crash evidence; original root cause unresolved
introduced: Carried from focused v0.9.70 Tk audit; status rechecked for v0.9.72

title: Destroyed Geo roots remain strongly owned by traces and selection subscriptions
cause: Raw destroy bypasses normal listener cleanup and variable trace callbacks retain the owner graph. Normal close removes the listener but does not prove every trace graph is released.
repro: Run probes/ownership_probe.py on v0.9.72: ten raw root destruction cycles, main-thread GC, then separate diagnostic listener/search/all-owner-trace removal controls.
expected: Disposed owners are releasable on their owner thread; fixtures do not carry obsolete roots into unrelated tests.
observed: Ten destroyed roots/listeners remain; removing listeners or search traces alone is insufficient; removing the remaining210 variable traces releases all ten. Diagnostic cleanup changes only disposable probe objects.
recommendation: Own each trace/subscription token and provide idempotent disposal for supported destruction paths. Do not blanket-delete all variable traces in production.
regression_risks: Normal close versus raw destroy, worker lifetime and fixture teardown; no proof this causes original SIGSEGV or leaks client processes after they exit.
confidence: High for retention; Low for SIGSEGV causality
classification: Confirmed retention on exercised path; possible native-crash contributor
introduced: Carried from focused v0.9.70 Tk audit; status rechecked for v0.9.72

title: Petro search trace retains destroyed application roots
cause: The variable trace retains a bound owner method after raw destruction.
repro: Run probes/petro_retention.py: ten raw destroy/GC cycles and diagnostic owner trace cleanup.
expected: No linear retention of disposed root graphs across repeated GUI lifecycle tests.
observed: Ten roots retained; removing ten trace commands releases all ten (16320 objects collected).
recommendation: Retain/remove the search trace token in owner disposal and exercise all termination paths.
regression_risks: Do not lose search/filter state or infer Windows customer memory leakage from a raw-destroy test alone.
confidence: High for retention; Low for SIGSEGV causality
classification: Confirmed retention on exercised path; possible contributor

title: Wrong-thread finalization remains a demonstrated native Tcl failure class
cause: The earlier isolated same-runtime probe proves a destroyed root cycle collected on a worker can panic Tcl without Workbench or Matplotlib. Existing main-thread fixture collection cannot collect graphs still strongly rooted by traces.
repro: Use the prior focused audit minimal_gc.py in disposable subprocesses; compare owner-thread collection with deliberate worker collection/allocation. This is a controlled negative test, not the original application crash.
expected: Application owners are deterministically disposed on their owning thread; workers hold plain data.
observed: Prior native stacks: Tk8.6.16 SIGABRT through Tcl_AsyncDelete/Tkapp_Dealloc; Tk9.0.4 SIGILL panic trap. Main controls pass. Neither signal is the reported SIGSEGV139.
evidence: prior focused Tk native traces; runtime-Tk86.json; runtime-Tk9.json
recommendation: Release Tk-containing graphs deterministically on their owner thread; keep the existing fixture guard as mitigation, not closure.
regression_risks: No global GC disabling; do not substitute this controlled panic for original SIGSEGV reproduction. The v0.9.72 application trigger remains unproved.
confidence: High for controlled native failure; Low for link to SIGSEGV
classification: Confirmed root cause of controlled panic only; original link unresolved
introduced: Carried from focused v0.9.70 Tk audit; status rechecked for v0.9.72

title: Geo destruction leaves startup and poll timers naming deleted Tcl commands
cause: Owner timers are not explicitly cancelled before destruction deletes their callback commands.
repro: Run probes/timer_probe.py: destroy a disposable Geo root, then inspect Tcl after info and info commands directly.
expected: No queued callbacks reference deleted owner commands after disposal.
observed: Two timers remain, startup_project and _poll_requests; both script_command_exists flags are false. No native fault is inferred.
recommendation: Store/cancel owner job IDs before command destruction and prevent rescheduling after disposal.
regression_risks: Startup delay, polling, unexpected close and parent/child cancellation ordering.
confidence: High for stale callbacks; Low for native causality
classification: Confirmed stale callback state; possible contributor

title: Repeated-root fixtures amplify lifecycle state left by earlier modules
cause: Tests repeatedly create roots, pump update and use raw destruction; strong graphs can outlive their fixture despite owner-thread GC. This differs from a desktop process ending on close.
repro: Compare the recorded fresh, ordered and long-process runs in the focused audit and this full serial run; inspect the direct teardown calls and current retention controls.
expected: Fixtures have explicit owner/worker/callback cleanup and serial stress remains meaningful.
observed: Current ten-cycle probes confirm retained roots. Test-order/finalization timing is a supported amplification hypothesis; no proof identifies this as the original SIGSEGV trigger.
evidence: retention logs; full-serial log; prior focused audit A-D logs
recommendation: Correct owner cleanup, assert weak-reference/callback baselines and keep a long serial stress job; subprocess isolation can contain independent groups but cannot prove a product fix.
regression_risks: Do not hide failures by weakening tests or replacing serial qualification with only isolated runs.
introduced: Carried from focused v0.9.70 Tk audit; status rechecked for v0.9.72

title: Embedded figure ownership still needs sequence-level qualification
function: Embedded canvas lifecycle; raster idle processing
cause: Embedded figures are not all tracked by pyplot Gcf. Long GUI processes can retain graphs through owners, and nested idle pumping changes finalization timing. No native Matplotlib fault was proved.
repro: Use actual Figure/canvas weak references and owner cleanup checks under the full GUI sequence, not only pyplot.close/Gcf.
expected: Owner/canvas/job counts return to defined baselines after close and owner-thread collection.
observed: Earlier focused audit:800 isolated section cycles ended with zero retained sections/Figures after GC; mixed sequence retained many graphs. Current full-run memory is recorded separately; it is not a new figure-count measurement.
evidence: prior focused Tk lifecycle/sequence evidence; full-serial resource logs; section-job-results.json
recommendation: Trace retained owners before changing canvas integration; qualify idle draw, toolbar, bindings and close during raster preparation on both toolkit versions.
regression_risks: Keep renderers independent; high-water RSS alone is not proof of a leak, and no evidence supports blaming a library by name alone.
confidence: Medium for ownership risk; Low for SIGSEGV cause
classification: Possible contributing factor; not a confirmed native library defect
